To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gamma-irradiation of fetal rat brain cells induces apoptosis that requires synthesis of new proteins and RNA, is associated with increased levels of p53, p21, Fos, and JunB mRNAs, and is characterized by a decreased Bax/Bcl-2 +Bcl-xL ratio.

low-dose gamma-irradiation of 17-day pregnant rats kills forebrain stem cells and elicits within 3 h a DNA fragmentation pattern characteristic of apoptosis, and this apoptosis is associated with activation or up-regulation of the p53, AP-1, and Bax/Bcl-2 + -xL systems.
radiation-eliciting apoptosis of fetal brain stem cells is associated with p53 system activation and an increase in the ratio of Bax:Bcl-2 +Bcl-xL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which ionizing radiation causes cell death in the mammalian fetal brain.
the molecular events associated with the rapid cell death of fetal forebrain stem cells induced by low doses of gamma radiation.
the mechanisms by which ionizing radiation kills fetal rat brain cells and how this process might be modulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gamma-radiation-induced apoptosis in the fetal brain is associated with specific mRNA elevations and decreases.

gamma-radiation-induced apoptosis in the fetal rat forebrain is associated with activation or up-regulation of p53 and the p53-regulated cell-cycle inhibitor, p21/Waf/Cip-1, and with increased ratios of Bax to the antiapoptosis proteins, Bcl-2, and Bcl-x(L).
gamma-irradiation induces a complex pattern of changes in gene expression that is consistent with apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
radiation-induced apoptosis in the developing brain is associated with a specific pattern of mRNA changes, including activation of the p21/Waf/Cip-1 gene.
radiation-induced apoptosis is a complex process that involves many molecular changes and that the p53 and AP-1 systems are likely to play important roles.

the radiation-induced cell death in fetal brain tissue has many molecular characteristics of apoptosis, including DNA fragmentation, and is accompanied by changes in the levels of mRNas that are consistent with a p53-dependent pathway to apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular events associated with radiation-induced apoptosis in the developing brain are not identical to those of apoptosis in adult brain or in other cell types.
the molecular characteristics of radiation-induced cell death in fetal rat brain cells are consistent with apoptosis.
low-dose irradiation of the fetal rat forebrain elicits apoptosis in the developing nervous system, and that this process is associated with specific mRNA elevations.
